title: Congruent Triangles: SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, and HL
seo_title: Congruent Triangles Worksheet: SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, HL and CPCTC (Geometry) | 100 Questions
standard_text: Explain how the criteria for triangle congruence (ASA, SAS, and SSS) follow from the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions.
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheet on congruent triangles: choose SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS or HL, corresponding parts, missing information and CPCTC with algebra. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS and HL prove triangles congruent. SSA and AAA do not.
key_sub: The order of the letters in △ABC ≅ △DEF shows which parts match.
body_html:
How it works

Two triangles are congruent if a sequence of rigid motions maps one onto the other. Then all six pairs of corresponding parts are congruent. You only need to check three of them with a shortcut:

  • SSS: three pairs of sides.
  • SAS: two sides and the angle between them.
  • ASA: two angles and the side between them.
  • AAS: two angles and a side not between them.
  • HL: right triangles with congruent hypotenuses and one pair of congruent legs.

AAA and SSA do not prove congruence. In a congruence statement such as △ABC ≅ △DEF, the order of the letters shows which parts match. Look for hidden parts: a shared side (Reflexive Property) and vertical angles.

Example

△PQR ≅ △XYZ. Which side is congruent to QR?

Q ↔ Y and R ↔ Z

Answer: YZ

Example

∠A ≅ ∠D, ∠B ≅ ∠E and BC ≅ EF. Which shortcut?

The side BC is not between ∠A and ∠B

Answer: AAS

Common mistakes

  • Using SSA or AAA. They do not prove triangles congruent.
  • Mixing up ASA and AAS. Check whether the side is between the two angles.
  • Matching letters out of order. In △ABC ≅ △DEF, B matches E, not F.
  • Forgetting the shared side or the vertical angles that the figure gives for free.

faq.q: What are the five ways to prove triangles congruent?
faq.a: SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS and HL (for right triangles).

faq.q: Why doesn't SSA prove triangles congruent?
faq.a: Two different triangles can have two equal sides and an equal angle that is not between them, so the parts do not fix one triangle.

faq.q: What is the difference between ASA and AAS?
faq.a: In ASA the congruent side is between the two angles. In AAS the side is not between them.
Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are congruent. It is used after proving triangles congruent to show that other sides or angles are congruent.

items.q: Given △BXC ≅ △GDS, complete the statement: △XCB ≅ ?
items.e: Keep each pair of matching vertices together: X ↔ D, C ↔ S, B ↔ G. So △XCB ≅ △DSG.

items.q: Given △QVT ≅ △PER, which angle is congruent to ∠Q?
items.e: Q is in the same position as P in the statement, so ∠Q ≅ ∠P.

items.q: In △PQR and △XYZ, ∠R and ∠Z are right angles, and PQ ≅ XY (the hypotenuses). What else do you need to prove △PQR ≅ △XYZ by HL?
items.e: HL needs the hypotenuses and one pair of legs. PR and XZ are legs: PR ≅ XZ.

items.q: In △RST and △UVW, RS ≅ UV and ST ≅ VW. What else do you need to prove △RST ≅ △UVW by SSS?
items.e: SSS needs the third pair of sides: RT ≅ UW.

items.q: In △RST and △UVW, ∠R ≅ ∠U and ∠S ≅ ∠V. What else do you need to prove △RST ≅ △UVW by ASA?
items.e: ASA needs the side between the two angles. RS is between ∠R and ∠S: RS ≅ UV.

items.q: In △ABC and △DEF, ∠A ≅ ∠D and ∠B ≅ ∠E. What else do you need to prove △ABC ≅ △DEF by ASA?
items.e: ASA needs the side between the two angles. AB is between ∠A and ∠B: AB ≅ DE.

items.q: In △ABC and △DEF, ∠A ≅ ∠D and ∠B ≅ ∠E. What else do you need to prove △ABC ≅ △DEF by AAS?
items.e: AAS needs a side that is not between the two angles, such as BC: BC ≅ EF.

items.q: In △PQR and △XYZ, PQ ≅ XY and ∠Q ≅ ∠Y. What else do you need to prove △PQR ≅ △XYZ by SAS?
items.e: SAS needs the angle between the two sides. ∠Q is between PQ and QR: QR ≅ YZ.

items.q: In △ABC and △DEF, ∠C and ∠F are right angles, and AB ≅ DE (the hypotenuses). What else do you need to prove △ABC ≅ △DEF by HL?
items.e: HL needs the hypotenuses and one pair of legs. AC and DF are legs: AC ≅ DF.

items.q: In △GHI and △LMN, ∠I and ∠N are right angles, and GH ≅ LM (the hypotenuses). What else do you need to prove △GHI ≅ △LMN by HL?
items.e: HL needs the hypotenuses and one pair of legs. GI and LN are legs: GI ≅ LN.

items.q: In △JKL and △MNO, JK ≅ MN and ∠K ≅ ∠N. What else do you need to prove △JKL ≅ △MNO by SAS?
items.e: SAS needs the angle between the two sides. ∠K is between JK and KL: KL ≅ NO.

items.q: In △GHI and △LMN, ∠G ≅ ∠L and ∠H ≅ ∠M. What else do you need to prove △GHI ≅ △LMN by ASA?
items.e: ASA needs the side between the two angles. GH is between ∠G and ∠H: GH ≅ LM.

items.q: In △RST and △UVW, ∠R ≅ ∠U and ∠S ≅ ∠V. What else do you need to prove △RST ≅ △UVW by AAS?
items.e: AAS needs a side that is not between the two angles, such as ST: ST ≅ VW.

items.q: In △PQR and △XYZ, ∠P ≅ ∠X and ∠Q ≅ ∠Y. What else do you need to prove △PQR ≅ △XYZ by ASA?
items.e: ASA needs the side between the two angles. PQ is between ∠P and ∠Q: PQ ≅ XY.

items.q: In △JKL and △MNO, ∠J ≅ ∠M and ∠K ≅ ∠N. What else do you need to prove △JKL ≅ △MNO by ASA?
items.e: ASA needs the side between the two angles. JK is between ∠J and ∠K: JK ≅ MN.

items.q: In △RST and △UVW, ∠T and ∠W are right angles, and RS ≅ UV (the hypotenuses). What else do you need to prove △RST ≅ △UVW by HL?
items.e: HL needs the hypotenuses and one pair of legs. RT and UW are legs: RT ≅ UW.

items.q: In △PQR and △XYZ, PQ ≅ XY and QR ≅ YZ. What else do you need to prove △PQR ≅ △XYZ by SSS?
items.e: SSS needs the third pair of sides: PR ≅ XZ.

items.q: In △JKL and △MNO, ∠J ≅ ∠M and ∠K ≅ ∠N. What else do you need to prove △JKL ≅ △MNO by AAS?
items.e: AAS needs a side that is not between the two angles, such as KL: KL ≅ NO.

items.q: In △GHI and △LMN, GH ≅ LM and HI ≅ MN. What else do you need to prove △GHI ≅ △LMN by SSS?
items.e: SSS needs the third pair of sides: GI ≅ LN.

items.q: In △RST and △UVW, RS ≅ UV and ∠S ≅ ∠V. What else do you need to prove △RST ≅ △UVW by SAS?
items.e: SAS needs the angle between the two sides. ∠S is between RS and ST: ST ≅ VW.

items.q: In △PQR and △XYZ, ∠P ≅ ∠X and ∠Q ≅ ∠Y. What else do you need to prove △PQR ≅ △XYZ by AAS?
items.e: AAS needs a side that is not between the two angles, such as QR: QR ≅ YZ.

items.q: In △JKL and △MNO, ∠L and ∠O are right angles, and JK ≅ MN (the hypotenuses). What else do you need to prove △JKL ≅ △MNO by HL?
items.e: HL needs the hypotenuses and one pair of legs. JL and MO are legs: JL ≅ MO.

items.q: △JKL ≅ △MNP. JL = 3x − 9 and MP = 2x. Find MP.
△GHK ≅ △LMN. m∠H = 54°, m∠K = 52° and m∠L = (4x + 38)°. Find x.
items.e: ∠L corresponds to ∠G, so m∠G = 180 − 54 − 52 = 74. Then 4x + 38 = 74, so x = 9.

items.q: △JKL ≅ △MNP. m∠J = 53°, m∠K = 47° and m∠P = (4x + 24)°. Find x.
items.e: ∠P corresponds to ∠L, so m∠L = 180 − 53 − 47 = 80. Then 4x + 24 = 80, so x = 14.

items.q: △JKL ≅ △MNP. m∠J = 75°, m∠L = 32° and m∠N = (5x + 13)°. Find x.
items.e: ∠N corresponds to ∠K, so m∠K = 180 − 75 − 32 = 73. Then 5x + 13 = 73, so x = 12.

items.q: △ABC ≅ △DEF. AB = 5x − 3 and DE = x + 29. Find DE.
△PQR ≅ △XYZ. m∠P = 49°, m∠R = 69° and m∠Y = (2x + 34)°. Find x.
items.e: ∠Y corresponds to ∠Q, so m∠Q = 180 − 49 − 69 = 62. Then 2x + 34 = 62, so x = 14.

items.q: △ABC ≅ △DEF. BA = 2x + 10 and ED = 6x − 10. Find ED.
△RST ≅ △UVW. RT = 3x − 22 and UW = 14. Find x.
items.e: Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are congruent (CPCTC): RT = UW, so 3x − 22 = 14 and x = 12.

items.q: △RST ≅ △UVW. ST = 4x − 26 and VW = 2x − 6. Find VW.
△PQR ≅ △XYZ. m∠Q = 48°, m∠R = 69° and m∠X = (4x + 31)°. Find x.
items.e: ∠X corresponds to ∠P, so m∠P = 180 − 48 − 69 = 63. Then 4x + 31 = 63, so x = 8.

items.q: △ABC ≅ △DEF. m∠B = 73°, m∠C = 45° and m∠D = (3x + 23)°. Find x.
items.e: ∠D corresponds to ∠A, so m∠A = 180 − 73 − 45 = 62. Then 3x + 23 = 62, so x = 13.

items.q: △RST ≅ △UVW. RT = 4x + 10 and UW = 26. Find x.
items.e: Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are congruent (CPCTC): RT = UW, so 4x + 10 = 26 and x = 4.

items.q: △JKL ≅ △MNP. KJ = 5x − 29 and NM = 11. Find x.
items.e: Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are congruent (CPCTC): KJ = NM, so 5x − 29 = 11 and x = 8.

items.q: △RST ≅ △UVW. m∠S = 56°, m∠T = 51° and m∠U = (5x + 13)°. Find x.
items.e: ∠U corresponds to ∠R, so m∠R = 180 − 56 − 51 = 73. Then 5x + 13 = 73, so x = 12.

items.q: △JKL ≅ △MNP. m∠J = 77°, m∠L = 59° and m∠N = (6x + 20)°. Find x.
items.e: ∠N corresponds to ∠K, so m∠K = 180 − 77 − 59 = 44. Then 6x + 20 = 44, so x = 4.

items.q: △GHK ≅ △LMN. KH = 5x + 21 and NM = 6x + 19. Find NM.
△ABC ≅ △DEF. CA = 2x + 2 and FD = 20. Find x.
items.e: Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are congruent (CPCTC): CA = FD, so 2x + 2 = 20 and x = 9.

items.q: △JKL ≅ △MNP. m∠K = 65°, m∠L = 60° and m∠M = (5x + 5)°. Find x.
items.e: ∠M corresponds to ∠J, so m∠J = 180 − 65 − 60 = 55. Then 5x + 5 = 55, so x = 10.

items.q: △PQR ≅ △XYZ. PQ = 2x + 16 and XY = 6x + 8. Find XY.
△ABC ≅ △DEF. BC = x + 25 and EF = 28. Find x.
items.e: Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are congruent (CPCTC): BC = EF, so x + 25 = 28 and x = 3.

items.q: △RST ≅ △UVW. m∠S = 62° and m∠W = 45°. Find m∠U.
items.e: ∠S matches ∠V, and ∠W matches ∠T. The third angle is 180 − 62 − 45 = 73°.

items.q: Is AAA a way to prove two triangles congruent?
c: No, because triangles have only two angles
Yes, if the angles are acute
No, because the triangles can be different sizes
items.e: Two equilateral triangles with sides 2 and 5 have the same angles but are not congruent. No, because the triangles can be different sizes.

items.q: Segments AC and BD bisect each other at M. Which shortcut proves △AMB ≅ △CMD?
items.e: AM ≅ CM and BM ≅ DM. ∠AMB ≅ ∠CMD because they are vertical angles, and that angle is between the two pairs of sides: SAS.

items.q: △CAB ≅ △FDE. AB = 20, BC = 13 and AC = 15. What is the perimeter of △DEF?
items.e: Congruent triangles have congruent corresponding sides, so the perimeters are equal: 20 + 13 + 15 = 48.

items.q: △HGK ≅ △MLN. m∠G = 85° and m∠N = 32°. Find m∠M.
items.e: ∠G matches ∠L, and ∠N matches ∠K. The third angle is 180 − 85 − 32 = 63°.

items.q: △TRS ≅ △WUV. RS = 6, ST = 15 and RT = 10. What is the perimeter of △UVW?
items.e: Congruent triangles have congruent corresponding sides, so the perimeters are equal: 6 + 15 + 10 = 31.

items.q: In the figure, which shortcut proves △ABD ≅ △CBD?
items.e: AB ≅ CB and AD ≅ CD are marked. BD ≅ BD by the Reflexive Property (a shared side). Three pairs of sides: SSS.

items.q: △JKL ≅ △MNP. JK = 17, KL = 11 and JL = 12. What is the perimeter of △MNP?
items.e: Congruent triangles have congruent corresponding sides, so the perimeters are equal: 17 + 11 + 12 = 40.

items.q: △ABC ≅ △DEF. Which must be true?
c: The triangles have the same orientation
items.e: All corresponding sides are equal, so the perimeters are equal. Orientation can change with a reflection. The perimeters are equal.

items.q: △QRP ≅ △YZX. m∠Q = 63° and m∠Z = 30°. Find m∠X.
items.e: ∠Q matches ∠Y, and ∠Z matches ∠R. The third angle is 180 − 63 − 30 = 87°.

items.q: Is SSA a way to prove two triangles congruent?
c: No, because two different triangles can have the same SSA parts
Yes, it is the same as SAS
No, because a triangle has no SSA parts
items.e: The angle is not between the sides, so the third side can swing to two places. No, because two different triangles can have the same SSA parts.

items.q: △KGH ≅ △NLM. GH = 13, HK = 13 and GK = 6. What is the perimeter of △LMN?
items.e: Congruent triangles have congruent corresponding sides, so the perimeters are equal: 13 + 13 + 6 = 32.

items.q: △CAB ≅ △FDE. m∠A = 51° and m∠F = 47°. Find m∠E.
items.e: ∠A matches ∠D, and ∠F matches ∠C. The third angle is 180 − 51 − 47 = 82°.

items.q: △KGH ≅ △NLM. GH = 8, HK = 11 and GK = 5. What is the perimeter of △LMN?
items.e: Congruent triangles have congruent corresponding sides, so the perimeters are equal: 8 + 11 + 5 = 24.

items.q: Two triangles are congruent if one can be mapped onto the other by
c: A sequence of dilations and translations
items.e: Congruence is defined by rigid motions (translations, reflections, rotations), which keep sizes the same. A sequence of rigid motions.

items.q: △CAB ≅ △FDE. AB = 11, BC = 10 and AC = 5. What is the perimeter of △DEF?
items.e: Congruent triangles have congruent corresponding sides, so the perimeters are equal: 11 + 10 + 5 = 26.

items.q: △GKH ≅ △LNM. m∠H = 40° and m∠N = 75°. Find m∠L.
items.e: ∠H matches ∠M, and ∠N matches ∠K. The third angle is 180 − 40 − 75 = 65°.

items.q: △ABC ≅ △DEF. m∠B = 66° and m∠F = 80°. Find m∠D.
items.e: ∠B matches ∠E, and ∠F matches ∠C. The third angle is 180 − 66 − 80 = 34°.

items.q: Why is HL a special case that works for right triangles?
c: HL is the same as SSA for all triangles
The hypotenuse is always the shortest side
The Pythagorean theorem fixes the third side
Right angles are always congruent, so any two parts work
items.e: With the hypotenuse and one leg, the other leg is determined, so it becomes SSS. The Pythagorean theorem fixes the third side.

items.q: △KGH ≅ △NLM. m∠G = 70° and m∠N = 73°. Find m∠M.
items.e: ∠G matches ∠L, and ∠N matches ∠K. The third angle is 180 − 70 − 73 = 37°.
